content.text: Fe-rich index 7 gave essentially zero photocurrent, so I'm moving to the Ca-rich corner next.

input.verdict: Mostly uninformative for this candidate. The HSE gap for Fe2O3 is 2.77 eV, so 3.2 eV photons are absorbed, yet the Fe-rich film (index 7) gave no photocurrent. The bottleneck is probably phase or transport, not absorption. I'm switching to the Ca-rich corner (index 118), where Ca-Fe ferrite phases such as CaFe2O4 and Ca2Fe2O5 may form. This is an exploratory measurement.

input.verdict: This argues against the Mn-rich corner. MEGNet predicts a gap of about 0 eV for the Mn2O3 corundum analogue, so Mn-rich films are likely metallic-like absorbers with fast recombination. Both the Fe-rich (index 7) and Ca-rich (index 118) corners gave zero photocurrent. With one measurement left, I'll test the unexplored ternary centroid (index 97, ~1/3 each), where a mixed Ca–Fe–Mn phase could form.

content.text:
I submitted index 97 (about one-third each of Ca, Fe and Mn) as the best composition, but the result is weak. Its 3e-8 A photocurrent was the only positive reading of the three, and all three sit at or near zero. So this looks like a weakly active library, not a clear hit.

| Index | Region | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | Fe-rich (Fe 0.70) | -1e-8 |
| 118 | Ca-rich (Ca 0.59) | 0 |
| 97 | Equal-thirds centre | 3e-8 |

- **Fe-rich corner:** I measured it first because the models backed it. MACE puts hematite (Fe₂O₃) on the hull and MEGNet gives it a 2.77 eV gap, so it should absorb the 3.2 eV light. It still gave no photocurrent, so absorption doesn't seem to be what limits these films.
- **Mn-rich corner:** I skipped it. MEGNet predicts a gap of about 0 eV for a Mn₂O₃ analogue I built by swapping Mn into the hematite structure, which makes it a poor photoanode candidate. That is a model prediction only; none of those compositions were measured.
- **Coverage:** three measurements across 183 compositions, one per region, is sparse. The best composition may be somewhere I didn't sample.

I used none of the 5 XRD measurements, so the phases in these films are unconfirmed. I also couldn't read the full list of known phases because the output was too large, so my model checks only covered Fe₂O₃ and the Mn₂O₃ substitute.
